hotels.title: The Danna Langkawi Resort & Beach Villas

meta.title: The Danna Langkawi Resort & Beach Villas | 1524 Delhi
meta.description: A colonial-style luxury resort on the shores of the Andaman Sea in Langkawi, Malaysia.

hotels.content:
The Danna Langkawi is a luxury colonial-style resort located on the north-western tip of Langkawi island, on the shores of the Andaman Sea. Built in the style of a 1920s colonial mansion, the resort offers 125 elegant rooms, suites and beach villas with spectacular views of the sea or the lush tropical gardens.

The resort features four dining venues including The Planter's, Turmeric, The Straits, and The Verandah, each offering unique dining experiences. Leisure facilities include a free-form infinity pool, a private marina, and a full-service Mandara Spa.

hotels.location_detail: Located on the northwest tip of Langkawi island on the shores of the Andaman Sea. The nearest airport is Langkawi International Airport, approximately 15 minutes away.

hotels.title: Pelangi Beach Resort & Spa

meta.title: Pelangi Beach Resort & Spa | 1524 Delhi
meta.description: A beachfront resort on the golden shores of Langkawi, Malaysia, surrounded by ancient rainforest.

hotels.content:
Pelangi Beach Resort & Spa is a beachfront retreat nestled between ancient rainforest and the golden shores of Cenang Beach, Langkawi. The resort is a village of 51 Malay-style chalets and villas that combine traditional architecture with modern comforts.

The resort is home to the Pelangi Spa, multiple dining outlets, and a range of water sports and leisure facilities. Its beachfront location on Cenang Beach — one of Langkawi's most popular beaches — offers direct access to the warm waters of the Andaman Sea.

hotels.title: Antara River Cruises

meta.title: Antara River Cruises | 1524 Delhi
meta.description: Luxury river cruises along India's sacred and historic waterways — the Ganges, Hooghly, and Mahanadi rivers.

hotels.content:
Antara Luxury River Cruises offers a unique way to experience India's sacred and historic waterways. The fleet sails along the Ganges, Hooghly, and Mahanadi rivers, connecting some of India's most culturally rich cities including Kolkata, Varanasi, and the temples of Orissa.

The ships are designed to reflect the rich cultural heritage of the regions they traverse, offering an intimate, all-inclusive luxury experience. Each vessel features tastefully appointed cabins, fine dining, onboard cultural performances, and curated shore excursions led by expert local guides.

hotels.title: Diphlu River Lodge

meta.title: Diphlu River Lodge | 1524 Delhi
meta.description: A boutique jungle lodge on the banks of the Diphlu River within Kaziranga National Park, Assam.

hotels.content:
Diphlu River Lodge is an intimate boutique jungle lodge set on the southern banks of the Diphlu River, within the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Kaziranga National Park in Assam. The lodge offers an unparalleled wildlife experience in the heart of one of India's most biodiverse national parks — home to the world's largest population of the endangered one-horned rhinoceros.

The lodge features 12 luxury cottages and tents blending harmoniously with the surrounding jungle. Guests enjoy jeep safaris, elephant safaris, boat rides, and guided nature walks led by expert naturalists.

hotels.title: Lahé Life Houseboat Cruise on the Brahmaputra River

meta.title: Lahé Life Houseboat Cruise on the Brahmaputra | 1524 Delhi
meta.description: A luxury houseboat cruise on the mighty Brahmaputra River through the pristine landscapes of Assam.

hotels.content:
Lahé Life is a luxury houseboat experience on the Brahmaputra River — one of Asia's mightiest and most majestic rivers. Departing from Guwahati in Assam, the houseboat navigates through pristine river islands (chars), national parks, and tribal villages that are rarely accessible by road.

'Lahé' means 'slowly' in Assamese — perfectly capturing the ethos of this unhurried, immersive journey. The houseboat features beautifully appointed cabins, a sun deck, and a team of expert naturalists and cultural guides to enrich every moment of the journey.

accommodation.name: Premium Cabin

hotels.title: The Nautilus

meta.title: The Nautilus | 1524 Delhi
meta.description: An ultra-luxury private island resort in the UNESCO Biosphere Reserve of Baa Atoll, Maldives.

hotels.content:
The Nautilus is an ultra-luxury boutique resort on Thiladhoo Island in the UNESCO Biosphere Reserve of Baa Atoll, Maldives. With just 26 houses and beach and ocean residences, The Nautilus offers exceptional privacy and personalised service in a setting of rare natural beauty.

Unlike traditional Maldivian resorts, The Nautilus operates on a 'freestyle luxury' philosophy — no set meal times, no fixed activity schedules, everything is personalised to each guest's rhythm. Each residence features a private pool, personal chef, and a dedicated 'Nautilus Host' (butler) available 24 hours.

hotels.title: The Strand Yangon

meta.title: The Strand Yangon | 1524 Delhi
meta.description: One of Asia's most iconic colonial heritage hotels, The Strand has been the address of choice in Yangon since 1901.

hotels.content:
The Strand Yangon is one of Asia's most storied colonial heritage hotels, established in 1901 by the Sarkies Brothers — the same family behind Raffles in Singapore and The Eastern & Oriental in Penang. Located in the heart of downtown Yangon on Strand Road, it has been the address of choice for royalty, statesmen, and literary greats for over a century.

The hotel has been meticulously restored to its original colonial grandeur, featuring 31 individually appointed rooms and suites. The Strand Bar, one of Yangon's most legendary venues, is famous for its colonial atmosphere and classic cocktails. The Strand Café and The Strand Restaurant complete the dining offering.

hotels.title: The Blackbuck Lodge

meta.title: The Blackbuck Lodge | 1524 Delhi
meta.description: An intimate wildlife lodge at the edge of Velavadar Blackbuck National Park in Gujarat.

hotels.content:
The Blackbuck Lodge is a small, intimate wildlife lodge located at the boundary of the Velavadar Blackbuck National Park in the Bhavnagar district of Gujarat. The park is home to the largest population of blackbuck antelope in India, as well as wolves, nilgai, and an extraordinary congregation of migratory birds including the lesser florican and harrier.

The lodge features just 12 tastefully appointed rooms designed to blend with the surrounding grassland landscape. The experience here is unhurried and immersive — game drives, bird walks, and naturalist-led treks through one of India's most underrated wildlife sanctuaries.

hotels.title: Ananda in the Himalayas

meta.title: Ananda in the Himalayas | 1524 Delhi
meta.description: An award-winning luxury destination spa in the Himalayan foothills, set on a 100-acre Maharaja's Palace Estate.

hotels.content:
An award-winning luxury destination spa in the Himalayan foothills, Ananda is located on a 100-acre Maharaja's Palace Estate. Surrounded by graceful Sal forests, overlooking the spiritual town of Rishikesh and the Ganges river valley, Ananda integrates traditional Ayurveda, Yoga, and Vedanta with international wellness experiences, fitness, and healthy organic cuisine to restore balance and harmony.

Ananda was voted World's Best Destination Spa by Condé Nast Traveller UK in 2005, 2006, 2007 and 2012, and by Condé Nast Traveller India in 2013, 2014, 2015 and 2017. It was also voted Best Spa for Mind, Body and Spirit, Yoga and Healthy Cuisine at the Spa Finder Wellness Travel Awards 2015.

hotels.title: Ahilya by the Sea

meta.title: Ahilya by the Sea | 1524 Delhi
meta.description: A boutique heritage property on the shores of Goa, owned by the Prince of Maheshwar.

hotels.content:
Ahilya by the Sea is a boutique retreat on the shores of Goa, owned by Prince Richard Holkar — son of the legendary Rani Ahilya Holkar of Maheshwar. Continuing the family tradition of heritage hospitality, this intimate property offers just a handful of individually decorated rooms and an immersive experience of Goa's culture, cuisine, and coastline.

The property reflects the owner's personal aesthetic — rich in art, antiques, and a carefully curated sense of place. Dining is a communal affair, with meals prepared from local and organic ingredients served in beautiful garden settings.

hotels.title: Ahilya Fort

meta.title: Ahilya Fort | 1524 Delhi
meta.description: An 18th-century riverside fort converted into a boutique heritage hotel in Maheshwar, Madhya Pradesh.

hotels.content:
Ahilya Fort is a magnificent 18th-century riverside fort on the banks of the Narmada River in Maheshwar, converted into a boutique heritage hotel by Prince Richard Holkar. The fort was the seat of power of the legendary queen Rani Ahilya Bai Holkar, one of India's most revered rulers, who transformed Maheshwar into a centre of culture, trade, and spiritual life.

The property offers just 12 individually designed rooms and suites filled with antiques, heirlooms, and personal artefacts. Dining is a centrepiece experience, with guests eating together on the fort's riverside terrace by candlelight. Boat rides on the Narmada, temple visits, and weaving village tours are among the curated activities.

villasAndEstates.title: Villa in the Woods at RAAS Devānya

meta.title: Villa in the Woods at RAAS Devānya | 1524 Delhi
meta.description: A hidden eco-conscious three-bedroom homestay nestled in the hills between Bhimtal and Mukteshwar, Uttarakhand.

villasAndEstates.content:
Welcome to The Villa in the Woods, a hidden gem nestled amidst the serene beauty of the hill slopes between Bhimtal and Mukteshwar. This enchanting three-bedroom homestay is part of the larger Devānya project, which embraces sustainable engineering and an eco-conscious lifestyle.

At The Villa in the Woods, you can escape the hustle and bustle of city life and immerse yourself in the tranquility of nature. Surrounded by lush greenery and breathtaking views, this retreat offers a unique opportunity to go off the grid while still enjoying the luxuries you're accustomed to.

Indulge in a culinary journey as you savour a blend of international, Kumaoni, and Rajasthani home-cooked delicacies. The meals are prepared using seasonal organic produce and grains sourced from Devānya's own organic farms or local farmers, guaranteeing freshness and sustainability.

posts.title: The Art of Slow Travel: Why India's Rivers Are Best Explored by Boat

meta.title: The Art of Slow Travel: India's Rivers by Boat | 1524 Delhi
meta.description: Why the most profound way to experience India is to slow down, board a boat, and let the river guide you.

posts.content: There is a particular kind of stillness that descends when you are on a river in India. The banks slide past — ghats, temples, jute mills, fishing villages, the call of a peacock from behind a curtain of reeds — and time becomes elastic. This is the gift of slow travel by boat: not a list of sights checked off, but a gradual immersion into the rhythm of a civilisation.

posts.title: Kaziranga: The Last Stronghold of the One-Horned Rhinoceros

meta.title: Kaziranga: Last Stronghold of the One-Horned Rhino | 1524 Delhi
meta.description: An inside look at Kaziranga National Park — one of India's greatest conservation success stories.

posts.content: In the tall elephant grass of the Brahmaputra flood plains, a shape materialises — vast, prehistoric, improbable. The one-horned rhinoceros of Kaziranga is one of nature's great survivors, brought back from the brink of extinction through one of India's most remarkable conservation stories. Today, the park is home to over two-thirds of the world's entire one-horned rhino population.

posts.title: Ahilya Fort: Where History Lives and Breathes

meta.title: Ahilya Fort: Where History Lives and Breathes | 1524 Delhi
meta.description: An intimate portrait of Ahilya Fort in Maheshwar — a living heritage property that honours one of India's most remarkable queens.

posts.content: There are places in India where history is not a museum exhibit but a lived, breathing reality. Ahilya Fort in Maheshwar is one such place. On the banks of the Narmada River, in a fort built by and named for the legendary queen Rani Ahilya Bai Holkar, guests dine by candlelight on the riverside terrace, sleep in rooms furnished with centuries-old heirlooms, and wake to the sound of temple bells drifting across the water.
